hypotheses.title: Recent deployment to payment-api (v2.8.1)
hypotheses.summary: The strongest temporal correlation. Error rate increased 4 minutes after v2.8.1 was released, /checkout became the most affected endpoint, and no dependency showed saturation.

evidence.label: Deployment v2.8.1 at 14:02
evidence.detail: payment-api v2.8.1 released 4 minutes before the first error signal.

evidence.label: Error rate +38%
evidence.detail: HTTP 500 rate increased 38% after deployment; /checkout most affected.

evidence.label: Temporal correlation tight (+4m)
evidence.detail: Error onset followed the deployment window by ~4 minutes.

evidence.label: Database latency stable
evidence.detail: PostgreSQL p95 stayed at ~190ms during the window.

evidence.label: Redis healthy
evidence.detail: Cache hit rate 99.1% and latency ~12ms.

evidence.label: CPU / memory normal
evidence.detail: payment-api CPU ~66%, memory ~61%; no saturation.

evidence.label: Connection resets in authorize step
evidence.detail: authorize failed with 'connection reset' against postgres-primary.

counterEvidence.label: No code diff observed on authorize path
counterEvidence.detail: v2.8.1 touched checkout retry backoff; not the authorize code directly.

hypotheses.title: Redis connection degradation
hypotheses.summary: Alternative hypothesis: connection pool warnings appeared before the error spike, but Redis itself reported healthy cache hit rates.

evidence.label: Pool warnings at 14:05
evidence.detail: Checkout-sessions pool at 78% usage.

counterEvidence.label: Redis latency healthy
counterEvidence.detail: ~12ms p50, 99.1% hit rate during the window.

hypotheses.title: Redis session cache miss storm on auth-api
hypotheses.summary: Session validation fell back to source lookups after the session cache hit rate collapsed, multiplying p95. Cache warming at 13:40 restored latency to baseline, which confirms the cache path as the cause.

evidence.label: Cache miss logged at 13:20
evidence.detail: session validation reported cache miss and took 640ms.

evidence.label: Trace shows 642ms stuck in cache.get
evidence.detail: sp-au3 lookup session on redis-cache accounts for 70% of the total span.

evidence.label: Postgres source lookup healthy
evidence.detail: read session row returned in 231ms, ruling out the database as the bottleneck.

evidence.label: Warming the cache resolved it
evidence.detail: After m.silva warmed session-cache at 13:40, p95 dropped to ~96ms.

evidence.label: No deploy in the window
evidence.detail: No auth-api deployment between 13:00 and 14:35, so no code change triggered this.

counterEvidence.label: Redis server itself stayed fast
counterEvidence.detail: redis-cache p50 latency held at ~12ms with healthy CPU; the miss rate, not Redis speed, is the problem.

hypotheses.title: Traffic spike on the auth path
hypotheses.summary: Alternative hypothesis: a burst of logins could stretch the connection pool. Log volume and error rate stayed flat, so this is unlikely.

evidence.label: Concurrent validations elevated
evidence.detail: checkout-sessions pool reached 78% consumption during the window.

counterEvidence.label: Error rate stayed low
counterEvidence.detail: auth-api error rate peaked at ~1.3%, well within tolerance for a capacity problem.

hypotheses.title: Full index rebuild degraded catalog search
hypotheses.summary: The rebuild started at 12:30 makes freshly indexed segments unsearchable, so queries return partial results. The degradation predates the rebuild, which points at the earlier index refresh as the trigger rather than the rebuild itself.

evidence.label: Search p95 degraded at 12:05
evidence.detail: Catalog search p95 exceeded 800ms, before the rebuild was triggered.

evidence.label: Trace shows unsearchable segment
evidence.detail: index.query returned 'rebuilding in progress' for the search-indexer span.

evidence.label: Index rebuild in progress
evidence.detail: A. Kumar triggered a full index rebuild at 12:30.

evidence.label: Still degraded in the current window
evidence.detail: catalog-api p95 holds around 640ms and error rate near 1.9%.

counterEvidence.label: Onset predates the rebuild
counterEvidence.detail: Latency was already above 800ms at 12:05, 25 minutes before the rebuild started, so the rebuild is not the sole cause.

hypotheses.title: search-indexer backlog starving the query path
hypotheses.summary: Alternative hypothesis: the indexer still lags behind kafka-bus, so segments are missing at query time. This is a real contributing factor and overlaps with INC-2388.

evidence.label: Indexer lag reported earlier
evidence.detail: Consumer lag on search-indexer was already a known problem resolved in INC-2388.

counterEvidence.label: Indexer lag is at zero
counterEvidence.detail: INC-2388 resolved the consumer group imbalance; lag returned to 0 at 10:12.

hypotheses.title: Consumer group imbalance on search-indexer
hypotheses.summary: Partitions were unevenly assigned across indexer replicas, so a subset of partitions went unconsumed and the index went stale. Rebalancing at 09:55 restored full coverage.

evidence.label: Lag growing from 09:30
evidence.detail: Consumer lag on partition 4 climbed steadily from 12000 messages.

evidence.label: Revoked assignment in trace
evidence.detail: poll batch failed with 'rebalance in progress'; index.apply saw 'assignment revoked'.

evidence.label: Rebalance fixed it
evidence.detail: Partitions were rebalanced at 09:55 and lag returned to 0 by 10:12.

evidence.label: kafka-bus itself healthy
evidence.detail: Broker throughput and latency were normal, isolating the fault to the consumer side.

hypotheses.title: Indexer replica CPU saturation
hypotheses.summary: Alternative hypothesis: replicas were CPU-bound and could not keep up. Resource usage stayed well below saturation.

evidence.label: Backlog implies slow consumption
evidence.detail: A growing lag is consistent with under-provisioned consumers.

counterEvidence.label: CPU far from saturation
counterEvidence.detail: search-indexer CPU never exceeded ~28% during the incident window.
